    10	/-!
    11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
    14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
    15	
    16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
    17	
    18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
    19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
    20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
    21	anywhere in the statement.
    22	
    23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
    24	
    25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
    26	
    27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
    28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
    29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
    30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
    31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
    32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
    33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
    34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
    35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
    36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
    37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
    38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
    39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
    40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
    41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
    42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
    43	
    44	## What this buys, stated exactly
    45	
    46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
    47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
    48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
    49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
    50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
    51	this tree.
    52	
    53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
    54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
    55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
    56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
    57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
    58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
    59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
    60	
    61	## What this does NOT do
    62	
    63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
    64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
    65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
    66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
    67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
    68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
    69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
    70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
    71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
    72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
    73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
    74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
    75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
    76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
    77	
    78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
    79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
    80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
    81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
    82	
    83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
    84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
    85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
    86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
    87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
    88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
    89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
    90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
    91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
    92	
    93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
    94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
    95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
    96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
    97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
    98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
    99	
   100	## Main declarations
   101	
   102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
   103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
   104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
   105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
   106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
   107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
   108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
   109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
   110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
   111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
   112	  arbitrary field.
   113	-/

   115	set_option autoImplicit false
   116	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
   117	
   118	universe u
   119	
   120	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
   121	
   122	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   123	
   124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   125	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   126	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
   127	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
   128	
   129	noncomputable section
   130	
   131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
   132	
   133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
   134	
   135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
   136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
   137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
   138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
   139	`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.
   140	
   141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
   142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
   143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
   147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
   148	  rfl
   149	
   150	/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/
   151	
   152	/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**
   153	
   154	`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
   155	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
   156	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.
   157	
   158	This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
   159	rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
   160	at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
   161	theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   162	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   163	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
   164	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
   165	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
   166	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
   167	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩
   168	
   169	/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
   170	`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
   171	datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.
   172	
   173	So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
   174	surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
   175	theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   176	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
   177	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   178	    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
   179	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   180	      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
   181	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
   182	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
   183	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
   184	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩
   185	
   186	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   187	
   188	/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/
   189	
   190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
   191	class, at genus `0`.
   192	
   193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
   194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
   195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
   196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
   197	and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
   198	triviality at genus `0`.
   199	
   200	The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
   201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
   202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
   203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
   206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
   208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
   214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
   215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
   218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
   220	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :=
   221	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   222	  refine D.fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero hg p ?_
   223	  rw [D.cechPicClass_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
   224	    relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField C B p]
   225	  exact classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented C lam D.cechPicClass h _
   226	
   227	/-! ## The engine, with no fibrewise hypothesis -/
   228	
   229	/-- **The rigid engine from a `pic⁰` membership**: `H¹(C_B, F_D) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F_D)` finite
   230	projective over `B`, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
   231	
   232	No fibrewise clause appears in the statement: the hypotheses are the membership, its
   233	presentation, and the engine's own `IsNoetherianRing B`. -/
   234	theorem rigidEngine_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) [IsNoetherianRing B]
   235	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   236	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   237	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   238	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass)) :
   239	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) ∧
   240	      Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) ∧
   241	      Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   242	  D.rigidEngine_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h)
   243	
   244	/-- **`π_*L` IS INVERTIBLE, FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP** — the stalk rank of `H⁰` is `1` at every
   245	prime of the test ring, for a cocycle-presented degree-zero class at genus `0`.
   246	
   247	This is the cohomological output the classical seesaw argument consumes next.  What it does not
   248	supply is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`; see the module docstring. -/
   249	theorem rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   250	    [IsNoetherianRing B] (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) (hg : genus C = 0)
   251	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
   252	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
   253	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
   254	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
   255	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   256	  D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_genus_zero hπ hg (D.htriv_of_pic0 hg lam h) p
   257	
   258	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# THE PRODUCER: `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` for a class in the image of the sheafification unit
    10	
    11	## What this file closes
    12	
    13	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean` proves CHART-U(b) at a general test from a per-affine-piece
    14	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`, and its header says plainly what it does not do:
    15	
    16	> The hypothesis is a *per-affine-piece existence of a datum with the plus-class property*, and
    17	> nothing here produces such a datum.
    18	
    19	**This file produces one**, and the ingredient that was missing is smaller than four successive
    20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
    21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
    22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
    23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity
    24	on this lane is an identity between a class pulled along `Over.testPoint` and one pulled along
    25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
    26	it they are the same class.
    27	
    28	## The shape of the producer, and its one genuine restriction
    29	
    30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
    31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
    32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes
    33	from `exists_cechPicClass_eq` applied to any Čech representative.
    34	
    35	That restriction is real and is named `IsPlusHonest` below.  It is **not** vacuous and **not**
    36	automatic:
    37	
    38	* not automatic — a general plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`,
    39	  and `Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is precisely the record that it becomes honest only over
    40	  `E.Carrier`, not over `A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is a genuine hypothesis, not a restatement;
    41	* not vacuous, and this is the payoff — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a **subgroup**, and every
    42	  class the chart layer twists by is in it: the θ-family (`thetaFamily_isPlusHonest`), the
    43	  Σ-family, and the Abel value itself (`abelDiv_isPlusHonest`).  So `chartTwist` preserves
    44	  honesty, and CHART-U(b) becomes **unconditional** on exactly the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart reads.
    45	
    46	  **A CORRECTION TO THIS PARAGRAPH, from a fresh-context review of the commit that first wrote
    47	  it, and it is the same failure this leaf recorded one round earlier.**  When first committed the
    48	  sentence above cited `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` **and that declaration did not exist** — a
    49	  workspace-wide grep returned exactly one hit, the sentence itself.  That is precisely the
    50	  failure mode r7 diagnosed (`docstring-declaration-lists-unchecked`) and filed a lesson about,
    51	  reproduced by the very session that filed it, inside its own *non-vacuity* argument.
    52	  A kernel check, a `sorry` census and an axiom probe are all silent about it.
    53	
    54	  It also mattered mathematically, which is why it was worth writing rather than deleting: the
    55	  θ- and Σ-witnesses are the **twist factors**, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest` discharges anyway,
    56	  so they say nothing about the class being *charted*.  Since `chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹`,
    57	  honesty of a chart value reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` alone — so `abelDiv_isPlusHonest` was
    58	  carrying the whole of the final clause.  It is now proved (below), so the paragraph stands as
    59	  written; had it not been, the honest statement would have been "no residue beyond
    60	  `IsPlusHonest lam`", with the Σ-chart clause unproved.
    61	
    62	## Main declarations
    63	
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.testPoint_eq_overSpecMap` — **the comparison**: on an affine test the
    65	  canonical field point is the base-change morphism.
    66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt` — the producer, with the datum given.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` — **the producer proper**: for a
    68	  class in the image of the unit, a datum with the plus-class property EXISTS.
    69	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsPlusHonest` — the per-affine-piece form, closed under the group operations.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest` — **CHART-U(b) with no residue** for an
    71	  honest class, and `chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest` the same open as DATA.
    72	-/

    74	set_option autoImplicit false
    75	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/

    80	universe u
    81	
    82	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    83	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
    84	
    85	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    86	
    87	open AlgebraicJacobian
    88	
    89	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    90	
    91	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    92	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    93	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    94	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    95	
    96	noncomputable section
    97	
    98	/-! ## The comparison: on an affine test the field point IS the base change -/
    99	
   100	/-- **On an affine test, the canonical field point is the base-change morphism.**
   101	
   102	`Over.testPoint t : overSpec k κ(t) ⟶ overSpec k A` is built from mathlib's

   154	/-! ## Reducing the residue to B-4's own named obligation
   155	
   156	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:321`'s docstring says the general-test statement follows from the
   157	affine one "by the affine-piece locality of the (b-amendment)'s transport (iii)", and adds that
   158	it "is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis *per affine
   159	piece*".  That is right, and this is the statement it describes. -/

   162	variable (C π) in
   163	/-- **The `haff` residue from a per-affine-piece presentation** — the link
   164	`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`'s docstring describes and does not state.
   165	
   166	For each affine open `U` of the test, a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `Γ(T.left, U)` presenting
   167	the restricted twisted class gives openness of the locus on that piece
   168	(`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation`), and `chartLocus` over the piece *is* that set
   169	by definition (`chartLocus` unfolds to the split-witness set of the twisted class, and the
   170	twist commutes with restriction by `picEtMap_chartTwist`).
   171	
   172	So the affine-local residue is **exactly** B-4's presentation obligation, quantified over
   173	affine pieces — no extra geometry, and in particular nothing certificate- or divRep-gated.

   178	`isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation` carries.  `IsFinite π` is strictly stronger than
   179	the file-level `IsAffineHom π` (whence the overlapping-instance warning, disabled below): the
   180	affine openness route runs through the rigid engine, which needs finiteness, while the rest of
   181	this file needs only affineness. -/

   183	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)

   153	
   154	variable (C π) in
   155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of
   156	record that is not landed, stated exactly.
   157	
   158	Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the
   159	twisted family `chartTwist C m Z _ λ` restricted to the test), a presentation is a
   160	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
   161	with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.
   162	
   163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
   164	
   165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
   166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
   167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
   168	  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
   169	  other route may use this theorem immediately;
   170	* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
   171	  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
   172	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
   173	  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
   174	  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
   175	  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
   176	  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
   177	  well as unusable. -/
   178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
   180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
   181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
   182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
   183	
   184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
   185	
   186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
   187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
   188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
   189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
   190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
   191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
   192	
   193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
   194	
   195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
   196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
   197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
   198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
   199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
   200	
   201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
   202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
   203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
   204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
   207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
   208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
   210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
   211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
   212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
   213	    apply Spec.map_injective
   214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
   215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
   216	  rw [h]
   217	  rfl
   218	
   219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
   220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
   221	
   222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
   223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
   224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
   225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
   226	particular along an isomorphism.
   227	
   228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
   229	
   230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
   231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
   232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
   233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
   234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
   235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
   236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
   237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
   238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
   239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
   240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
   241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
   242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
   243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
   244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
   245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
   246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
   248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
   250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
   251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
   252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
   253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
   255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
   256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
   257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
   258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   259	                    D.cechPicClass
   260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
   262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
   263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
   264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
   265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
   268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
   271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
   272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
   274	  rw [hset]
   275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ

   278	
   279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
   280	
   281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
   282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
   283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
   284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
   285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
   286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
   287	
   288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
   289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
   290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
   291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
   292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
   293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
   294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
   298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   299	  (hpres t).symm

   303	variable (C π) in
   304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
   305	over an affine test).
   306	
   307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
   308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
   309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
   310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
   311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
   312	
   313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
   314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
   315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
   316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
   317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
   318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis

   321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
   325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
   327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
   328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
   329	  -- other pointwise.
   330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
   332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
   334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
   335	  rw [hset]

    12	# DAT-C C2 — the rank-1 H⁰ export and the generator kit
    13	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-3 Σ-RANK1, §2 (N1)/(N3))
    14	
    15	On the fibrewise h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization
    16	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the datum engine's `H⁰` is an **invertible** module: finite,
    17	projective, and of stalk-rank exactly `1`.  This is the rank export the engine
    18	(`datumRigidEngine`, `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean`) leaves open — it delivers
    19	finite + projective, never `rankAtStalk = 1`.
    20	
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_relCurve` — the χ transport `χ(𝒪_{C_L}) = 1 − n` to every
    22	  field `L` of the test tower (base-field invariance of the genus, `chi_moduleKSheaf`
    23	  + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the private lemma of `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`).
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one` — **the fibre
    25	  computation**: for a datum whose fibre class over `L` has `classDeg = n`, with `H¹` of
    26	  the base-changed sheaf vanishing, `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1` — the Riemann–Roch anchor
    27	  `h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` (`n + (1 − n)`) read through the presentation
    28	  bridge `presentationSheafIso`.  The fibre geometric package is threaded as instance
    29	  arguments (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`).
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` — **Σ-RANK1,
    31	  the datum-level export**: on the vanishing locus (fibre degree `n`, `χ = 1 − n`),
    32	  `Module.rankAtStalk (H⁰(F_D)) p = 1`.  Route: `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as
    33	  the `κ(p)`-fibre dimension; `datumH0BaseChange` (on the nose) identifies the fibre with
    34	  `H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`; the fibre computation above pins it at `1`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one` — the
    36	  certified-family specialization (**N1**): for `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus
    37	  `V`, the divisor datum `D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has invertible `H⁰`.  The
    38	  fibre-degree hypothesis is discharged uniformly by `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass` (the
    39	  fibre class has `classDeg = n` at every field).
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum`
    41	  — **N3, the generator kit**: since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of rank `1` (hence has a
    42	  nontrivial fibre at every prime of the locus), a fibrewise-nonzero **global** section
    43	  exists Zariski-locally (`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`).
    44	
    45	Noetherian discipline (worksheet §2): every rank statement carries `[IsNoetherianRing S]`
    46	through the engine; the arbitrary-test consumers reach it through RE-5 stages.

     9	/-!
    10	# The chart locus SUPPLIES GAP-2's binders rather than needing them
    11	
    12	Seven files cite the keystone by name (measured, case-insensitively, at HEAD: `Pic0ChartLocus`,
    13	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce`, `Pic0ChartPair`, `Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective`, `Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce`,
    14	`JacobianDataAbelDegreeWindow`, and `RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness` itself); the chart-layer
    15	ones name the *relative form of DAT-C GAP-2* as the residue of
    16	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` (`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`; that file is
    17	**outside this one's import closure**, so the name is unresolvable here and is cited by
    18	location rather than bare — `I-1173`), and price its field-level keystone
    19	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)
    20	as landed-but-unfed: what a lane still owes, they say, are that keystone's three binders
    21	`hD`, `hD'` (effectivity) and `hone` (`h⁰ = 1`).
    22	
    23	**On the chart locus all three are consequences.**  The reason is visible in the definition
    24	and was apparently never read off it: `chartLocus` is *defined* by the very vanishing the rank
    25	anchor consumes.  `IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) asserts, at a point, the
    26	existence of a finite separable `L/κ(t)`, a presenting Čech class `M`, and a `CurveDivisor W`
    27	in that class with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`.  So membership already carries a divisor with
    28	`h¹ = 0`; what it does not carry is that divisor's *degree*, and the degree comes from
    29	outside, from the chart-index constraint.
    30	
    31	## The chain, every link landed before this file
    32	
    33	1. `classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff` (`Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean:85`) reads the
    34	   `L`-degree of the presenting class as the plus-degree of the class it presents;
    35	2. the twist ledger (`chartTwist` unfolded through `degAt_mul`/`degAt_inv`/
    36	   `degAt_thetaFamily_pow`/`degAt_sigmaFamily`) turns that into `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`, which the
    37	   chart-index constraint `hdeg` makes exactly `n`;
    38	3. `chi_relCurve_baseField` transports `χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` to the base-changed curve;
    39	4. the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`
    40	   (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives `h⁰ = deg + χ = n + (1 − n) = 1`;
    41	5. `exists_effective_of_h0_pos` (`RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean:175`) then produces an
    42	   **effective** divisor of the same class, so effectivity is free too;
    43	6. `h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` (`RiemannRoch/ClassCohomology.lean:89`) carries the
    44	   `h⁰` value across to it.
    45	
    46	## What this is NOT
    47	
    48	* It is **not** `hb_forces_h0_eq_one` (`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean:180`).  That takes a
    49	  *threshold* hypothesis — every divisor of degree `≥ n` has `H¹ = 0` — which its own file
    50	  proves **false** at `n = g` (a moving degree-`g` family has `h⁰ ≥ 2`).  Nothing here assumes
    51	  a threshold: the vanishing is supplied by the locus at **one** divisor, the one the
    52	  membership witness names.  A statement about one divisor of degree `n` is not a statement
    53	  about all of them, and only the former is true.
    54	* It does **not** discharge `exists_factor`, and therefore closes no antecedent of
    55	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  Everything here is **fibrewise**: it lives over a splitting
    56	  field `L/κ(t)` at a single point `t`.  Per the standing caveat of
    57	  `Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean`, uniqueness of the *fibre* witness is not injectivity of
    58	  the chart at a general test — the gap measured as `RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar`
    59	  (`Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean:237`, also outside this file's closure).  What is removed is
    60	  one *named input* of the field-level keystone, not the relativisation.
    61	* `n = genus C` is **not** proved here and is not assumed either: `n` is whatever the chart
    62	  index is legal at, and `hχ : χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is a hypothesis.  Per `I-1176`,
    63	  `chi_moduleKSheaf` *converts* that pinning rather than supplying it, so the binder stays
    64	  explicit and its supplier stays named.
    65	
    66	## Main declarations
    67	
    68	* `h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg` — the rank anchor at a witness of the pinned degree.
    69	* `exists_splitting_h0_eq_one_of_mem_chartLocus` — **the converse of
    70	  `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`**: from locus membership, a witness with `h⁰ = 1`.
    71	* `eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_of_subsingleton` — the keystone with `hone` discharged.
    72	* `exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one` — effectivity is free once `h⁰ = 1`.
    73	* `existsUnique_effective_of_mem_chartLocus` — **the payoff**: at a locus point the class has
    74	  an effective representative that is the unique one, with all three keystone binders supplied.
    75	-/

name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute

    52	The proof rests on a body of quasi-coherent descent, developed here from scratch and of
    53	independent use: on `Spec R` a quasi-coherent sheaf of modules is the `tilde` of its global

    55	quasi-compact quasi-separated open — and pushforward along a quasi-compact quasi-separated
    56	morphism preserves quasi-coherence. The file also builds the annihilator ideal sheaf, the
    57	schematic support and the rank-`d` local freeness predicate for sheaves of modules on a scheme,

   120	/-! ## The Hilbert polynomial of a coherent sheaf
   121	
   122	The Hilbert polynomial `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.hilbertPolynomial` is constructed in
   123	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.HilbertPolynomial` (imported above): it is the unique
   124	`Φ_{F,s} ∈ ℚ[λ]` agreeing for `m ≫ 0` with the graded Hilbert function
   125	`m ↦ dim_{κ(s)} Γ(X_s, F_s ⊗ L_s^{⊗m})` of the fibre section module. This is the `H⁰`-only
   126	encoding; it agrees with the Euler-characteristic form `χ(F(m))` by Serre vanishing, for
   127	proper `X_s` and ample `L_s`. See `Scheme.hilbertPolynomial_eq_of_eventually` for uniqueness
   128	and `Scheme.existsUnique_hilbertPolynomial_of_isRatHilb` for existence, the latter resting on
   129	the graded Hilbert–Serre theorem of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GradedHilbertSerre`.
   130	
   131	Reference: Nitsure §1; cf. Hartshorne III.5.2. -/
   132	
   133	/-! ## The Quot functor, the Grassmannian, and representability
   134	
   135	The functor definitions `Scheme.QuotFunctor` and `Scheme.Grassmannian` — Setoid quotients of
   136	families of quotients, with their pullback functoriality — and the representability statements
   137	`Scheme.Grassmannian.representable` and `Scheme.QuotScheme` live in
   138	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.QuotFunctorDef`. That functor-of-points layer consumes the
   139	flattening-stratification flatness predicate `Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat`, the support and
   140	freeness predicates built below in this file, and the Hilbert-function machinery of
   141	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.HilbertPolynomial`, so it sits above this file,
   142	`FlatteningStratification` and `GlueDescent` in the import order. -/
   143	end Scheme

   145	/-! ## Cohomology and base change
   146	
   147	The Quot construction uses cohomology and base change in two places: the boundedness step
   148	(Nitsure §5, "Use of m-regularity") and the Grassmannian embedding (Nitsure §5, "Embedding
   149	Quot into Grassmannian").
   150	
   151	Stacks 02KH states flat base change for all higher direct images `R^i f_*` of quasi-coherent
   152	sheaves. What is proved here is the `i = 0` form on `Scheme.Modules`, the substantive content
   153	of part (ii) of that statement; the `R^i` form for `i ≥ 1` is not proved. -/
   154	
   155	/-! ### Flat base change of cohomology (Stacks tag 02KH, `i = 0` form)
   156	
   157	Let
   158	```
   159	   g'
   160	X' ───→ X
   161	│       │
   162	f'      f
   163	↓       ↓
   164	S' ───→ S
   165	   g
   166	```
   167	be a cartesian square of schemes with `g` flat and `f` quasi-compact
   168	quasi-separated. Let `F` be a sheaf of `O_X`-modules. Then the canonical
   169	base-change map `g* (f_* F) ⟶ f'_* ((g')* F)` is an isomorphism in
   170	`S'.Modules`.
   171	
   172	(The full Stacks 02KH statement covers all higher direct images
   173	`R^i f_* F` for `i ≥ 0`; what is proved here is the `i = 0` form, the
   174	substantive content of part (ii) of that statement.)
   175	
   176	The base-change natural transformation itself is the mate of the
   177	`pullback ⊣ pushforward` adjunction (Mathlib's `mateEquiv` applied to
   178	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction`); that it is an isomorphism
   179	is `canonicalBaseChangeMap_isIso`. The deep content (Stacks 02KH / 02KE /
   180	00H8) lies entirely in that step: it reduces affine-locally to the claim
   181	that, for a flat ring map `A → B`, the canonical map
   182	`B ⊗_A H^i(X, F) → H^i(X_B, F_B)` is an isomorphism for quasi-coherent
   183	`F`, here in its `i = 0` form. The affine-local reduction runs through the
   184	section formula of Stacks 01HQ (`pullback_app_isoTensor`) and a
   185	quasi-compact open-cover Mayer–Vietoris induction. -/
   186	
   187	/-- The canonical base-change natural transformation `g* (f_* -) ⟶ f'_* ((g')* -)`
   188	associated to a cartesian square
   189	```
   190	     g'
   191	X' ─────→ X
   192	│         │
   193	f'        f
   194	↓         ↓
   195	S' ─────→ S
   196	     g
   197	```
   198	in `Scheme`. Constructed as the *mate* (Beck–Chevalley transform)
   199	under the `pullback ⊣ pushforward` adjunctions on sheaves of modules
   200	of the canonical 2-isomorphism
   201	`pullback g ⋙ pullback f' ≅ pullback f ⋙ pullback g'` coming from
   202	`g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g`.
   203	
   204	This natural transformation always exists (no flatness needed). The
   205	content of the flat base-change theorem (Stacks tag 02KH) is the
   206	*isomorphism* claim under the hypotheses
   207	`[QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Flat g]`; that claim is the
   208	helper `canonicalBaseChangeMap_isIso`. -/
   209	noncomputable def canonicalBaseChangeMap
   210	    {X X' S S' : Scheme.{u}}
   211	    {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}
   212	    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g) :

    36	  q.FiberH1Vanishing L t` ranges over *all* points of the underlying space of
    37	  `Spec A` (all primes), not only closed points.  For general noetherian `A`
    38	  (noetherian ≠ Jacobson: e.g. a DVR, whose generic point is contained in no
    39	  closed point's closure) the closed-point form is strictly weaker and the
    40	  engine's conclusion FAILS if the hypothesis is checked at closed points
    41	  only.  A finitely generated `k`-algebra *is* Jacobson, so on the pinned
    42	  base the two forms happen to agree — but (i) the reduction uses h¹ upper

   250	/-- The **fibrewise `h⁰`** of a sheaf of modules `L` on the total space of a
   251	family `q : X ⟶ S` at a point `t : S`: the dimension over the residue field
   252	`κ(t)` of the global sections of the restriction `L_t` of `L` to the
   253	scheme-theoretic fibre `X_t = q.fiber t`,
   254	
   255	`h⁰(t) = dim_{κ(t)} Γ(X_t, L_t)`.
   256	
   257	The `κ(t)`-structure is `Scheme.Hom.fiberSectionsModule` (restriction of
   258	scalars along `κ(t) → Γ(X_t, 𝒪)`), exactly the convention of
   259	`Scheme.hilbertFunction`; when the dimension is infinite, `Module.finrank`
   260	takes the junk value `0`.  This is the (P2-kit-independent) fibre `h⁰`
   261	vocabulary of campaign milestones B3/B5/B6/J1/J3. -/

   283	/-! ## §3. The B3 statement pins and the gate -/
   284	
   285	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   286	
   287	/-- **B3, step 1a (statement pin): rank-`χ` local freeness of the rigid
   288	pushforward** (Mumford AV II §5, Corollary 2; EGA III 7.9.9; Hartshorne III
   289	12.11; campaign milestone B3(i), first conclusion).
   290	
   291	For the constant curve `C_A = C ×_k Spec A` with projection
   292	`q = pullback.snd : C_A ⟶ Spec A` and every invertible sheaf `L` on `C_A`
   293	with `h¹(C_t, L_t) = 0` at **every scheme point** `t : Spec A` (see the
   294	module docstring for the quantifier audit), the pushforward `q_* L` is
   295	locally free with stalkwise rank the fibre dimension
   296	`h⁰(C_t, L_t) = χ(L_t)`: every point has an open neighbourhood `U` on which
   297	`(q_* L)|_U ≅ 𝒪_U^{⊕ h⁰(t)}`.
   298	
   299	The rank is pinned as `q.fiberH0 L t` (`= χ(L_t)` since `h¹ = 0`; the
   300	`χ`-ledger reformulation is the P3-interface TODO).  Local constancy of
   301	`t ↦ h⁰(L_t)` on `Spec A` is a *consequence* of this statement (the rank of
   302	a free module over a nontrivial ring is well defined on connected
   303	components), not a separate hypothesis.

   305	This `Prop` is honestly TRUE for every finitely generated (equivalently,
   306	noetherian quotient) `k`-algebra `A`; the gate `HasRigidPushforward`
   307	quantifies it exactly there.  Truth for *arbitrary* `A` is not claimed —
   308	that extension is milestone B2 (filtered colimits). -/
   309	def RigidPushforwardLocallyFree (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   310	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
   311	  ∀ L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules,
   312	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
   313	    (∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
   314	      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t) →
   315	    ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
   316	      ∃ U : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Opens, t ∈ U ∧
   317	        Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj
   318	            ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   319	              (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L) ≅
   320	          _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
   321	            (ULift.{u} (Fin ((pullback.snd C.hom
   322	              (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).fiberH0 L t))))
   323	
   324	/-- **B3, step 1b (statement pin): the formation of the rigid pushforward
   325	commutes with arbitrary base change** (Mumford AV II §5, Corollary 3;
   326	campaign milestone B3(i), second conclusion).

   328	Under the same hypotheses as `RigidPushforwardLocallyFree` (invertible `L`,
   329	`h¹(L_t) = 0` at all scheme points), for **every** commutative ring

   336	```

   340	     Spec A' ------Spec φ-----> Spec A

   347	def RigidPushforwardBaseChange (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   348	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] : Prop :=
   349	  ∀ L : (Limits.pullback C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).Modules,
   350	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L →
   351	    (∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),
   352	      (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)))).FiberH1Vanishing L t) →
   353	    ∀ (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] (φ : A →+* A'),

   355	        (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
   356	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))
   357	        (pullback.snd (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))
   358	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))
   359	        (pullback.fst (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))

   425	    (h1 : ∀ t : Spec (CommRingCat.of A),

   444	/-- **Rank-one local freeness gives local triviality** (scaffold brick for the
   445	B3 rank-one corollary): if every point of `X` has an open neighbourhood on
   446	which `M` pulls back to the free module of rank one, then `M` is an
   447	invertible sheaf in the project sense (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`:
   448	trivializations on an *affine* cover).  Proof: shrink each neighbourhood to

   450	trivialization along the inclusion (pullback pseudofunctor coherences +
   451	`pullbackFreeIso`), and identify the rank-one free module with the unit
   452	(`coproductUniqueIso`, as in `LineBundle.freeUnitIso`). -/
   453	theorem LineBundle.isLocallyTrivial_of_pointwise_free_one {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules)
   454	    (h : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧
   455	      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M ≅
   456	        _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)))) :
   457	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial M := by
   458	  intro x
   459	  obtain ⟨U, hxU, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h x
   460	  obtain ⟨W, hW_aff, hxW, hWU⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset hxU
   461	  have hle : W ≤ U := hWU
   462	  refine ⟨W, hxW, hW_aff, ⟨?_⟩⟩
   463	  have e₁ : M.restrict W.ι ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback W.ι).obj M :=
   464	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app M
   465	  have e₂ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback W.ι).obj M ≅
   466	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle ≫ U.ι)).obj M :=
   467	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (X.homOfLE_ι hle)).symm).app M
   468	  have e₃ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle ≫ U.ι)).obj M ≅
   469	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   470	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M) :=
   471	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (X.homOfLE hle) U.ι).app M).symm
   472	  have e₄ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   473	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj M) ≅
   474	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   475	        (_root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))) :=
   476	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).mapIso e
   477	  have e₅ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (X.homOfLE hle)).obj
   478	        (_root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))) ≅
   479	      _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) :=
   480	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackFreeIso (X.homOfLE hle) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1))
   481	  have e₆ : _root_.SheafOfModules.free (R := W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) ≅
   482	      _root_.SheafOfModules.unit W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
   483	    Limits.coproductUniqueIso (fun (_ : ULift.{u} (Fin 1)) ↦
   484	      _root_.SheafOfModules.unit W.toScheme.ringCatSheaf)
   485	  exact e₁ ≪≫ e₂ ≪≫ e₃ ≪≫ e₄ ≪≫ e₅ ≪≫ e₆

   491	corollary; Kleiman §5): if moreover `h⁰(C_t, L_t) = 1` at every scheme point
   492	`t : Spec A` (so `χ ≡ 1` given `h¹ ≡ 0`), the pushforward `q_* L` is an

   509	        (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))))).obj L) := by

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
